---
title: "Quiz · Cast the System"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. Why are characters described as "responsibilities in disguise"?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Each character maps to a responsibility in the system. A line of dialogue between
two characters is a way of explaining a system interaction. The teaching power
comes from this mapping, not from the character's personality.
:::

## 2. What is the recommended maximum cast size for an audio drama?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Five or six characters. In audio-only, the listener has no visual cues, so each
character must be distinguishable by voice alone. More than six becomes hard to
track.
:::

## 3. What is "breaking the fourth wall" in this context?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
An optional technique where a character briefly acknowledges its technical
counterpart (e.g. "Hello Developer — ahum, I mean Customer") to re-anchor the
listener to the architecture without abandoning the narrative. It should be used
sparingly.
:::

## 4. What are the six fields recorded for each character in characters.md?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Character, Technical counterpart, Responsibility, Personality, Voice, and
Relationship to other characters.
:::

## 5. Should a character exist without a responsibility?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No. Every character must trace back to the mapping in metaphor.md. No character
should be introduced purely for comic effect or flavour without a responsibility
behind it.
:::
